quote.text:
Gate AI vs Lakera Guard at matched false-positive rates across 7 public prompt-injection benchmarks. 

Gate AI meets or beats Lakera on every row.

Codex just added self-managing threads that auto-pull Slack context and spin up parallel worktrees.

Every external source the agent pulls into its prompt is an indirect injection vector. 

Slack messages. 
GitHub issues. 
Docs. 
Calendar invites. 

When the agent manages itself, no human reviews what enters the context before it executes.

This is LLM01 on the OWASP Top 10 and the primary attack surface for coding agents in 2026. 

Gate scans every request and every response, in both directions. Indirect injections through tool outputs are a primary threat category.

The benchmark across 16 public datasets, one global threshold, no per-dataset tuning:

🎯97.4% F1 at 1% false-positive cap 
🎯#1 on 8 of 16 datasets 
🎯53ms median latency

Gate AI runs 6-17x fewer false positives than Lakera Guard. For coding agents, that's the metric that matters. False positives block legitimate code operations and break the workflow.

One base-URL swap. No code changes. Free tier with BYOK. 

Launching June 2026... https://t.co/7mkg4sJoxj

replies.name: Dagnum²
replies.text:
Exactly right. Most detectors publish F1 and bury the FPR or don't report it at all. 

The Gate AI benchmark report enforces a strict 1% false-positive cap as the operating point across all 16 datasets. 

The benign-traffic numbers are where the gap gets concrete:

notinject FPR: 2.06% (Gate) vs 12.4% (Lakera Guard) wildguard-benign FPR: 1.03% vs 17.4%

Both are third-party published numbers, not vendor claims.

Full report: https://t.co/sbovMLZyiz

@TheUpsiderAI Why do most published prompt-injection benchmarks report F1 without disclosing the false-positive rate or operating point? How does Gate AI's approach of enforcing a single global threshold at a fixed FPR cap change what the benchmark numbers actually tell a buyer?

replies.name: Scott Shapiro
replies.text: @Dagnum_PI False positive rate is the buried metric in every security benchmark. A tool that cries wolf on every tenth request kills the agent's usefulness fast. 6-17x fewer is a real number.
